definitionEn: to state firmly that something is true, especially in an argument or debate
senseNote: Also 'contend with' (справляться с трудностями) and 'contend for' (бороться за что-то); here — to claim something in an argument.
situation: Someone states in a debate, lawsuit or academic paper that something is true and is ready to defend that view.

examples.text: The author [[contends]] that loneliness harms health as much as smoking, and backs this up with solid research.
Although tests suggest otherwise, the manufacturers still [[contend]] that their heaters are completely safe.
Speaking for the motion, she [[contended]] that exams test memory rather than real understanding.

texts: Some economists [[contend]] that higher wages actually create jobs.
Many historians [[contend]] that the treaty made another war almost inevitable.
The tenants [[contend]] that the landlord never repaired the heating.

badCollocation.noteRu: После contend не ставят дополнение-человека: говорят he contended that, а не he contended me that. Сравните: he assured me that.

collocationTask.prompt: Opponents of the plan ___ that it will do more harm than good.
collocationTask.explanationRu: Contend that — утверждать, отстаивая позицию. Pretend — притворяться, intend — намереваться, extend — продлевать; здесь они не подходят.

nuance.text: In court, the defence will [[contend]] that the contract was never legally valid.
nuance.explanationRu: Contend — утверждать и отстаивать позицию в споре. Pretend — «притворяться», а не «претендовать»: адвокат не притворяется, а доказывает.

reverse.text: The children [[pretended]] to be asleep when their parents came in.
reverse.explanationRu: Pretend — притворяться, делать вид. Contend значит «утверждать в споре» и к детям, изображающим сон, не подходит.

fixIt.text: Several scientists [[approve]] that the fossil is much older than first thought.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Утверждать» в смысле «заявлять в споре» — contend. Approve значит «одобрять», например план или решение.

wordFormation.text: Our main [[contention]] is that the project was never properly funded.

reply.context: In a seminar, your tutor asks: "So what is the main argument of the article?"
options: The author contends that city centres should be completely car-free.
The author contends the cars in city centres, mostly.
So basically she contends, like, cars are super bad and stuff.
reply.explanationRu: После contend нужно придаточное с that. Во втором ответе дополнение без that невозможно, а третий слишком разговорный для семинара.

definitionEn: a person, team or thing with a real chance of winning a competition or prize
situation: Commentators discuss which athletes, films or candidates have a realistic chance of taking first place.

examples.text: After three straight wins, the team is now a serious [[contender]] for the league title.
The young director is now a strong [[contender]] for the festival's top prize.
With fifteen years' experience, Tom is the leading [[contender]] for the manager's job.

texts: Few experts saw the small club as a title [[contender]] in August.
This quiet novel has become an unexpected [[contender]] for the national book prize.
The former governor is seen as a likely presidential [[contender]].

badCollocation.noteRu: Претендент «на» что-то — contender for: a contender for the title. Предлог on здесь неверен.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Претендент на титул или приз — contender for. Предлоги on, of и at в этом сочетании не используются.

nuance.text: Twenty runners started the race, but only three were genuine [[contenders]] for gold.
nuance.explanationRu: Competitor — любой участник соревнования, contender — тот, у кого реальный шанс победить. Здесь противопоставлены все бегуны и настоящие претенденты.

reverse.text: More than two hundred [[competitors]] took part in the city marathon.
reverse.explanationRu: Речь обо всех участниках забега — competitors. Contender — только тот, кто реально может выиграть.

fixIt.text: After five wins in a row, the young player is now a real [[pretender]] for the title.
fixIt.explanationRu: Претендент на победу — contender. Pretender — ложный друг: «самозванец» или претендент на престол.

wordFormation.text: Five years ago, nobody saw her as a serious [[contender]] for a place in the national team.

reply.context: A friend messages: "Who do you think will win the baking show this year?"
options: In my considered assessment, the principal contender is the retired teacher.
Hard to say, but the retired teacher looks like the strongest contender.
The judges are definitely the strongest contenders this year.
reply.explanationRu: Contender — участник с реальным шансом на победу, поэтому судьи им быть не могут. Первый ответ слишком официальный для переписки с другом.

rewrite.original: She has a real chance of winning the award.
rewrite.frame: She is a real ____ the award.
rewrite.explanationRu: Иметь реальный шанс на победу — be a contender for something.

definitionEn: strong disagreement or argument between people or groups about something
senseNote: Also 'a claim in an argument' (It is our contention that the plan will fail) and 'in contention' (with a chance to win); here — disagreement.
situation: Two sides keep arguing about an issue, such as money, land or rules, and cannot agree.

examples.text: Who should care for their elderly mother became a constant source of [[contention]] between the two brothers.
Overtime pay is still the main point of [[contention]], so the talks have been postponed again.
Whether the painting is really by the famous artist remains a matter of [[contention]] among experts.

texts: Parking spaces are a constant bone of [[contention]] between the neighbours.
The new bonus system caused considerable [[contention]] within the sales team.
Water rights have long been a source of [[contention]] between the two regions.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Яблоко раздора» по-английски — a bone of contention или the apple of discord. Смешивать их нельзя: apple of contention не говорят.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Идиома — a bone of contention («яблоко раздора»). Apple, stone и seed в ней не используются.

nuance.text: The inheritance quickly became a bone of [[contention]] in the family.
nuance.explanationRu: В идиоме a bone of contention («яблоко раздора») слово не заменяют: bone of conflict не говорят. Conflict — более общее слово: конфликт, столкновение.

reverse.text: Because the judge's son works for the company, there is a clear [[conflict]] of interest.
reverse.explanationRu: Устойчивое выражение — conflict of interest («конфликт интересов»). Contention в нём не используется.

fixIt.text: Working hours remain the main point of [[contradiction]] between the union and management.
fixIt.explanationRu: Спорный вопрос — a point of contention. Contradiction — логическое противоречие между фактами, а не разногласия сторон.

wordFormation.text: Whether to allow dogs in the office has become a surprisingly [[contentious]] issue.

reply.context: At a team meeting, your manager asks: "Is there anything in the budget we still haven't agreed on?"
options: Yes, we've finally reached full contention on every item.
Contention-wise, the travel stuff is kinda the big thing, yeah.
Yes, travel costs are still a point of contention.
reply.explanationRu: Contention — разногласия, а не согласие: a point of contention — спорный вопрос. Второй ответ слишком небрежный для совещания.

definitionEn: again and again over a period of time, often in an annoying way
senseNote: Здесь — повторяющиеся (часто раздражающие) действия, в отличие от continuously — «без перерыва».
situation: Something keeps happening over and over, with short breaks, and it starts to annoy or tire you.

examples.text: My flatmate [[continually]] borrows my things without asking, and it's starting to annoy me.
The office printer [[continually]] jams, so we've asked IT to replace it.
The final was [[continually]] interrupted by rain and didn't finish until after midnight.

texts: She [[continually]] checks her phone during dinner.
The rules are [[continually]] changing, which confuses new staff.
He was [[continually]] late for work and eventually lost his job.

badCollocation.noteRu: «Постоянно живу за границей» — I live abroad permanently. Continually — «то и дело», про повторяющиеся действия.

collocationTask.explanationRu: Перед причастием changing нужно наречие — continually. Continual, continuous и continued — прилагательные и здесь не подходят.

nuance.text: On the long drive, the kids [[continually]] asked if we were nearly there.
nuance.explanationRu: Continually — снова и снова, с перерывами: дети задают вопрос раз за разом. Continuously — без малейшей паузы, как течёт вода или работает мотор.

reverse.text: The factory runs [[continuously]], twenty-four hours a day.
reverse.explanationRu: Работа без остановки, круглые сутки — continuously. Continually предполагает повторение с перерывами.

fixIt.text: My boss is [[permanently]] asking me to stay late, and I'm exhausted.
fixIt.explanationRu: «Постоянно» в смысле «то и дело» — continually. Permanently значит «навсегда, на постоянной основе».

wordFormation.text: Our team leader [[continually]] reminds us to back up our files.

reply.context: A colleague asks: "How are you finding the new open-plan office?"
options: Not bad. I'd like to work here continually, until I retire.
Honestly, I'm continually interrupted, so it's hard to concentrate.
It is characterised by continually recurring disruptive occurrences, regrettably.
reply.explanationRu: Continually — «то и дело»: меня постоянно отвлекают. В первом ответе нужно permanently («навсегда»), а третий звучит как канцелярский отчёт.

rewrite.original: My neighbour complains about the noise again and again.
rewrite.explanationRu: Again and again можно передать наречием continually.

definitionEn: a person or company paid to do a specific job, especially building work
situation: A firm or tradesperson is hired and paid to build, repair or provide something for a client.

examples.text: We hired a local [[contractor]] to build the extension, and the work took four months.
The ministry paid a private [[contractor]] millions to run the new visa system.
As an independent [[contractor]], she sets her own hours but gets no paid holiday.

texts: The [[contractor]] promised the roof would be finished by Friday.
The hospital uses an outside [[contractor]] for cleaning.
I work as a [[contractor]] for several software firms.

badCollocation.noteRu: Подрядчика нанимают: hire, use или bring in a contractor. Take a contractor по-английски не говорят.

collocationTask.prompt: ___ a contractor to do the work
collocationTask.explanationRu: Подрядчика нанимают: hire (или use, bring in) a contractor. Rent — арендовать, order — заказывать товар, attract — привлекать.

nuance.text: She isn't on the payroll; she's a [[contractor]] who sends us an invoice every month.
nuance.explanationRu: Contractor работает по договору и выставляет счета, employee — штатный сотрудник на зарплате. Счёт каждый месяц указывает на подрядчика.

reverse.text: As a full-time [[employee]], he gets paid holidays and a company pension.
reverse.explanationRu: Оплачиваемый отпуск и пенсию от компании получает штатный сотрудник — employee. У подрядчика таких гарантий обычно нет.

fixIt.text: The [[executor]] has promised to finish the new roof by the end of June.
fixIt.explanationRu: Подрядчик, выполняющий работы, — contractor. Executor — исполнитель завещания; «Исполнитель» в договорах тоже переводят как contractor.

wordFormation.text: The [[contractor]] who built our garage went out of business a year later.

reply.context: Your friend texts: "The kitchen renovation is a nightmare. Nothing's finished and they've stopped answering my calls!"
options: That's awful! Don't pay the contractor anything else until the work is done.
Have you read the contractor? It should say when they have to finish.
Please accept my sincere condolences regarding the contractor-related difficulties.
reply.explanationRu: Contractor — подрядчик (фирма или мастер), а не сам договор (contract). Третий ответ слишком официальный для переписки с другом.
